look_here_first: Treat this as a taxon-concept check. Strict V. cinerea has angled hairy/cobwebby branchlets, cordate usually shallowly lobed leaves with visible gray-green lower surfaces, and small black berries that are only slightly glaucous.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: strict concept branchlets densely short-hairy and cobwebby

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: cordate leaves usually unlobed to shallowly 3-shouldered

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: lower leaf surface gray-green and visibly hairy rather than opaque white-felted

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: berries black, roughly 4–8 mm, slightly or not glaucous

lookalikes.differences: Central Texas Heller's grape should not be called V. cinerea simply because an app uses a broad concept; compare with V. berlandieri first.
